summary: Karl Felix Halm worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He taught Albert Grünwedel and held positions at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library from circa 1856 to 1882.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University in 1880. He later served as a professor at Uppsala University (~1899–1925) and taught Helmer Smith and Jarl Charpentier.

Karl Florenz specialized in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Georg von der Gabelentz, Ernst Windisch, Friedrich Max Müller, and Tetsujiro Inoue. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut, and University of Hamburg.

Karl Friedrich Geldner worked in Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin (from 1890), and Marburg (1907–1921).
Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College (~1952–1953), Harvard College (~1953–1956), and Harvard University (~1957–1966).

Karl H. Potter was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of California and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at the University of Minnesota, University of Washington, and as General Editor of the Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies.

Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, and held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983).

Karl Jettmar was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna and later held appointments at Weltmuseum Wien, University of Vienna, Mainz University, and Heidelberg University.

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the universities of Mainz and Würzburg, later holding positions at the Lyceum and Hofbibliothek in Aschaffenburg and as a professor at the University of Bonn from 1818.

Karl Lachmann was a scholar in linguistics who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815). He held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1851.

Karl Müllenhoff specialized in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University, the University of Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Kiel University (1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (1858).

Karl Otfried Müller was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf, and served as a professor at the University of Göttingen from 1819.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held positions at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), the London School of Economics, King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Richard Lepsius worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin, he held a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1846–1884) and served as Chief Librarian at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1873–1884).

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Heidelberg, studying under G. W. F. Hegel. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1831) and the University of Königsberg (1833).

Karl Verner was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under August Leskien, subsequently working as a librarian at Halle-Wittenberg (~1876–1883) and as a lecturer in Slavic studies at Copenhagen from 1882.
Karl von Hegel worked in history and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock from circa 1841 to 1856 and at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1856 to 1893.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Augsburg and the University of Munich, he held posts at Munich, the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy, and as professor at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He has held positions at Hamburg and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied as the main pupil under Anagarika Govinda (~1952–1985) and succeeded him in 1982.
